audits.title: Uses deprecated APIs
audits.description: Deprecated APIs will eventually be removed from the browser. [Learn more about deprecated APIs](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/best-practices/deprecations/).

audits.title: Uses third-party cookies
audits.description: Third-party cookies may be blocked in some contexts. [Learn more about preparing for third-party cookie restrictions](https://privacysandbox.google.com/cookies/prepare/overview).

audits.title: Reduce unused JavaScript
audits.description: Reduce unused JavaScript and defer loading scripts until they are required to decrease bytes consumed by network activity. [Learn how to reduce unused JavaScript](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/unused-javascript/).

audits.title: Issues were logged in the `Issues` panel in Chrome Devtools
audits.description: Issues logged to the `Issues` panel in Chrome Devtools indicate unresolved problems. They can come from network request failures, insufficient security controls, and other browser concerns. Open up the Issues panel in Chrome DevTools for more details on each issue.

audits.title: Use efficient cache lifetimes
audits.description: A long cache lifetime can speed up repeat visits to your page. [Learn more](https://web.dev/uses-long-cache-ttl/).

audits.title: Font display
audits.description: Consider setting [font-display](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/font-display) to swap or optional to ensure text is consistently visible. swap can be further optimized to mitigate layout shifts with [font metric overrides](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/font-fallbacks).

audits.title: LCP request discovery
audits.description: Optimize LCP by making the LCP image [discoverable](https://web.dev/articles/optimize-lcp#1_eliminate_resource_load_delay) from the HTML immediately, and [avoiding lazy-loading](https://web.dev/articles/lcp-lazy-loading)

audits.title: Network dependency tree
audits.description: [Avoid chaining critical requests](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/critical-request-chains) by reducing the length of chains, reducing the download size of resources, or deferring the download of unnecessary resources to improve page load.

audits.title: Serve static assets with an efficient cache policy
audits.description: A long cache lifetime can speed up repeat visits to your page. [Learn more about efficient cache policies](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/uses-long-cache-ttl/).

audits.title: Avoid enormous network payloads
audits.description: Large network payloads cost users real money and are highly correlated with long load times. [Learn how to reduce payload sizes](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/total-byte-weight/).

audits.title: Enable text compression
audits.description: Text-based resources should be served with compression (gzip, deflate or brotli) to minimize total network bytes. [Learn more about text compression](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/uses-text-compression/).

audits.title: Avoid serving legacy JavaScript to modern browsers
audits.description: Polyfills and transforms enable legacy browsers to use new JavaScript features. However, many aren't necessary for modern browsers. Consider modifying your JavaScript build process to not transpile [Baseline](https://web.dev/baseline) features, unless you know you must support legacy browsers. [Learn why most sites can deploy ES6+ code without transpiling](https://philipwalton.com/articles/the-state-of-es5-on-the-web/)

audits.title: Avoid an excessive DOM size
audits.description: A large DOM will increase memory usage, cause longer [style calculations](https://developers.google.com/web/fundamentals/performance/rendering/reduce-the-scope-and-complexity-of-style-calculations), and produce costly [layout reflows](https://developers.google.com/speed/articles/reflow). [Learn how to avoid an excessive DOM size](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/dom-size/).

audits.title: Legacy JavaScript
audits.description: Polyfills and transforms enable older browsers to use new JavaScript features. However, many aren't necessary for modern browsers. Consider modifying your JavaScript build process to not transpile [Baseline](https://web.dev/articles/baseline-and-polyfills) features, unless you know you must support older browsers. [Learn why most sites can deploy ES6+ code without transpiling](https://philipwalton.com/articles/the-state-of-es5-on-the-web/)
